 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jay Bothroyd didn't hold back his criticism of Leon Goretzka in Aston Villa's Carabao Cup defeat to Bournemouth on Wednesday. 
 The Villans were knocked out of the fourth round of the Carabao Cup after suffering a 3-0 defeat to the Cherries on the south coast.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement An early goal from Amine Adli set the tone for the hosts, as Villa failed to equalise before the break, despite having several chances.
 Marco Bizot was left with his head in his hands in the 51st minute after Lewis Cook's effort squirmed in from a tight angle before Alvaro Rodriguez tucked away Bournemouth's third.
 Unai Emery will now be fully focused on the Champions League and the Premier League for the rest of the campaign, as his side suffered their first loss in eight games at the hands of Bournemouth.
 Goretzka was handed his first start at the Vitality, but Bothroyd saw something that he didn't like for Aston Villa.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jay Bothroyd rips into Leon Goretzka in Aston Villa loss vs Bournemouth 
 While covering Villa's game on Sky Sports' Soccer Special, Bothroyd was left unimpressed by Goretzka's headed miss from a corner in stoppage time of the first half.
 He said: "That was their best chance; it's [Emi] Buendia. He's been creating havoc everywhere; he's pinged a ball in, and Goretzka's got on the end of it.
 "I don't know why he's headed it down; that is not a difficult header. He has to hit the target; it's a great delivery from Buendia.
 "Glenn [Murray], look at that. I can't believe that; it's a free header. He needs to be scoring; that's poor. He's played for some of the biggest clubs in the world."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Goretzka's effort had a minimal 0.03 xG, and it didn't even count as a "big chance missed", which shows just how much Bothroyd was overreacting.
 In fact, the midfielder was the highest-rated Villa player at the break, joint at 6.7 with Bizot, as the former had an impressive game in general.
 Bothroyd didn't react like that for anyone else, even though Villa racked up a whopping 1.65 in xG, missing four big chances in total.
 That means Goretzka's effort was just 1.8 per cent of Villa's overall xG tally.
 The former Bayern Munich star finished the game as Villa's highest-rated player, picking up a 7.2 FotMob score, completing the joint-most dribbles in the match (2), and boasting an impressive 97 per cent passing accuracy, too.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Aston Villa player ratings vs Bournemouth: Lamare Bogarde nowhere to be seen, 7/10 deserved more Does Goretzka deserve to keep his place now? 
 Joao Gomes and Goretzka were arguably two of Villa's better players against Bournemouth.
 After making his full debut, Goretzka has taken more steps towards earning his place in the starting eleven for the foreseeable future,
 However, the fact is that he was part of a team that lost its first game in eight matches.
 There were definite moments where you could see the Bayern Munich and German national team quality in the midfielder, but he needs to build his fitness up.
 Once Goretzka has more minutes under his belt, it feels inevitable that he'll have a starting spot nailed at Villa.
